key_insight: UniClawBench introduces a universal benchmark designed to evaluate proactive AI agents on realistic, multi-step everyday tasks rather than simplified sandbox scenarios. It aims to measure what these agents can actually do in real-world tool-using environments.
problem_solved: Existing agent benchmarks often rely on artificial environments and single-turn tasks, which do not capture the complexity of real-world tool use, long-horizon planning, and proactive behavior. They also mix multiple capabilities within one task taxonomy, making evaluation less precise and harder to interpret.
method: Defines a benchmark focused on proactive agents operating in real-world settings with everyday tools and tasks.
Uses task design and evaluation that better reflect multi-step interaction, planning, and autonomous execution.
Provides a more universal evaluation framework to separate and assess different agent capabilities more cleanly.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this benchmark offers a more realistic way to compare agent systems and identify true strengths and failure modes. It can help guide the development of agents that are more reliable, useful, and deployable in practical settings.
visual_elements: A comparison diagram showing sandbox benchmarks vs. real-world proactive tasks
A pipeline graphic of observe → plan → act → adapt
An evaluation matrix mapping tasks to capabilities such as planning, tool use, and autonomy
Icons representing everyday tools and user environments
paper_title: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
paper_authors: Zhekai Chen, Chengqi Duan, Kaiyue Sun, Bohao Li, Yuqing Wang
